subject: Request: Geo-standby activation lead-time & RPO deviation for FinWise proof-of-concept
messages:
From: Daniel Huang <daniel@finwise.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finwise.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Geo-standby lead time and RPO question for POC

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. Our compliance team asked a couple of follow-ups about multi-region failover behavior for the POC. Specifically: we need clarity on your warm-standby activation lead time (what you call "activation window") and whether you can commit to a 30‑minute RTO for cross-region switchover during the POC.

FinWise's ops mandate: 30‑minute activation and RPO <= 5 minutes for production, but for a short-term POC they'd accept a 2‑hour activation window if we can document the controls and runbooks.

Can Redwood provide an exception for the POC that documents:
- a defined maximum activation lead time for the hosted POC environment,
- an RPO commitment (or an explicit documented tolerance), and
- the steps you will take if we hit degraded replication during a switchover?

I attached the draft mutual action plan to help speed approvals.

Thanks,
Daniel
Head of Infrastructure — FinWise

Attachment: finwise-mup-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Huang <daniel@finwise.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo-standby lead time and RPO question for POC

Hi Daniel — really appreciate the clear ask and the M.A.P.

Short answer: for the standard hosted POC we cannot promise a production-grade 30‑minute cross-region activation universally, because our hosted POC runs on shared capacity and we rely on cold-to-warm transitions for some regions. That said, we're happy to propose a bounded exception for the POC with documented controls:

Proposal for POC (what Redwood can commit to):
- Activation lead time: <= 2 hours (documented runbook + cold-warm failover steps).
- RPO: best-effort replication with documented typical case <= 5 minutes; POC exception tolerance up to 30 minutes for delta during activation.
- Compensating controls: automated KV cache flush, asymmetric read routing during switchover, and a designated runbook owner on our side.

If FinWise needs the 30‑minute activation and strict 5‑minute RPO even for the POC, we'd need to move you to a short-term Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) during the POC or a scoped Private deployment — both of which require a brief procurement path.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Karthik runs a quick replication gap test and documents typical RPO distribution for your dataset (ETA 24–36 hours).
2) I'll draft a short POC SLA addendum that records the exception window and compensating controls.
3) If Procurement requires hard SLAs, loop in Naomi (legal) and Aditya (sales) so we can scope an expedited Dedicated proof commitment.

I've attached a SOC2 summary you'd asked for earlier for context.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Exec — Redwood Inference

Attachment: soc2-summary.pdf (PDF)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Huang <daniel@finwise.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo-standby lead time and RPO question for POC

On Tue, 18 Jun 2028 at 17:30, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> 
> Proposal for POC (what Redwood can commit to):
> - Activation lead time: <= 2 hours (documented runbook + cold-warm failover steps).
> - RPO: best-effort replication with documented typical case <= 5 minutes; POC exception tolerance up to 30 minutes for delta during activation.

Folks — I ran the replication-gap test against a sample FinWise workload this morning. Summary:
- Median replication lag: ~75 seconds for synthetic RL load.
- 95th percentile: ~6 minutes under simulated burst traffic and cross-region egress throttles.
- Cold-warm activation runbook measured on our test harness: 45–90 minutes end-to-end (including service handoff validation).

Notes and mitigations:
- We can reduce activation to ~30–45 minutes if FinWise agrees to a short warm-up run with pre-warmed caches (requires a lightweight Dedicated burst or scheduled warmup).
- RPO under normal conditions is comfortably below 5 minutes; worst-case during activation we observed spikes near 12–18 minutes with synthetic stress, not 30. We'll document test artifacts.

Action requested of Legal/Sales for an exception addendum:
- Naomi: can we record "POC exception — activation <= 2 hours; expected typical activation 45–90 minutes; RPO typical <=5 minutes; activation-time RPO tolerance <= 30 minutes" in a one-page addendum?
- Aditya/Neha: propose we include a clause describing the scope (hosted POC only), duration (90 days), and an escape hatch to convert to Dedicated within 7 business days if FinWise needs hard 30-min RTO.

I'll attach the raw test logs and a one-page runbook snippet to the thread.

Thanks,
Karthik
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachment: replication-test-logs.zip (archive)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Huang <daniel@finwise.com>, Procurement <procurement@finwise.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo-standby lead time and RPO question for POC

Hi all — reviewed Karthik's test summary and the proposed wording. Legal is comfortable documenting a scoped POC exception with explicit limits and compensating controls. Proposed addendum language (one-paragraph summary):

"Redwood Inference will provide a scoped POC exception for FinWise during the period of June 19, 2028 through September 17, 2028. For the scoped POC (hosted environment only), Redwood's activation lead time commitment shall be a maximum of two (2) hours. Redwood represents that typical activation in validated test conditions is expected to be 45–90 minutes. Redwood further represents that under normal replication conditions RPO for the POC environment will be 5 minutes or less; during activation events Redwood will use best efforts to contain data divergence with a documented tolerance of up to thirty (30) minutes for the duration of the activation event. This POC exception does not apply to production Dedicated or Private deployments. FinWise may request conversion to a Dedicated environment with hard SLAs, which will be subject to a separate commitment and procurement."

We will also add: runbook owner contact, test log links, and an adoption clause requiring FinWise to acknowledge the scope and duration. Once Neha/Aditya confirm, I'll produce the addendum PDF for signatures and attach the DocuSign link.

—Naomi
Chief Legal Officer — Redwood Inference

Attachment: poc-exception-draft.txt (text)
